passage:
A government website gave products repair scores. A higher score meant the item was easier to open, fix, and find parts for.
Consumers began comparing scores before buying phones, laptops, and appliances.
Some companies improved designs because customers cared.
Students discussed how information can influence markets. If buyers know only price and appearance, companies may ignore repair. If buyers see repair scores, durability becomes part of competition.
The score did not force people to choose repairable products, but it made the choice visible.
Transparency can change behavior without shouting. A small number on a label can push design in a better direction.
